'''Hutti Gold Mines Limited''' ({{langx|kn|(ರಾಯಚೂರು ಹಟ್ಟಿ ಚಿನ್ನದ ಗಣಿ}}) (HGML) is a company located in the state of [[Karnataka]], [[India]] and engaged in the [[mining]] and production of [[gold]]. It was first established as Hyderabad Gold Mines in 1947. With the closing of [[Kolar Gold Fields]] in 2001, it is one of the two companies in India which produce gold by mining and processing the gold ore, the other being Manmohan Minerals Industries Pvt. Ltd. Owned by the [[Government of Karnataka]], HGML has two plants located in [[Hutti]] and [[Chitradurga]]. HGML mines gold from its main gold mine located in [[Hatti Gold Mines|Hutti]] and other satellite mines.

==Executive==
The Company's Corporate Office is located in [[Bangalore|Bengaluru]].{{citation needed|date=July 2024}}

==Mining==
The mines managed by HGML are mainly located in the Hutti-Muski [[precambrian]] greenstone  belt which contains both readily extractable native gold and gold-bearing [[sulphide]]s.<ref name="mine">{{cite web|url=http://www.hinduonnet.com/thehindu/seta/2002/02/21/stories/2002022100060300.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20021220141351/http://www.hinduonnet.com/thehindu/seta/2002/02/21/stories/2002022100060300.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=20 December 2002|work=Online Edition of the Hindu, dated 2002-02-21|publisher=2002, The Hindu|title=Biotechnology in gold extraction|accessdate=2007-08-02}}</ref> HGML consists of two gold units:<ref name="unit">{{cite web|title=HGML Gold Mines|url=http://pib.nic.in/archieve/lreleng/lyr2003/rjul2003/30072003/r3007200313.html|work=Online webpage of the Press Information Bureau|publisher=Government of India|accessdate=2007-08-02}}</ref>
* Hutti Gold Unit: This consists of HGML's main mine located at Hutti and the satellite mines- Uti and Hirabuddini, all of which are located in the [[Raichur district]]. Hutti is an underground mine, Uti is an [[open-cast mine]] while Hirabuddini is an exploratory mine.
* Chitradurga Gold Unit: This consists of an open-cast mine located in Ajjanahalli in [[Tumkur district]] and an exploratory underground mine at G. R. Halli in [[Chitradurga district]].<ref name="fin">{{cite web|url=http://www.hinduonnet.com/thehindu/2002/01/17/stories/2002011703030300.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020427102942/http://www.hinduonnet.com/thehindu/2002/01/17/stories/2002011703030300.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=27 April 2002|work=Online Edition of The Hindu, dated 2002-01-17|title= Hutti Gold Mines becomes member of World Gold Council|publisher=The Hindu|accessdate=2007-08-01}}</ref>

These mines in total produce about 3 tonnes of gold a year.<ref name="mine"/> With the closure of the Bharat Gold Mines Limited which had operations at [[Kolar Gold Fields]] in Karnataka and at [[Chittoor district]] in [[Andhra Pradesh]], HGML is one of the only two companies in India that produce gold by mining.<ref name="pib">{{cite web|url=http://pib.nic.in/release/release.asp?relid=21478|work=Online webpage of the Press Information Bureau|title=Gold Production during April-September, 2006|publisher=Government of India|accessdate=2007-08-01}}</ref><ref name="mines">{{cite web|url=http://mines.nic.in/imsene.html|work=Online webpage of the Department of Mines|publisher=Government of India|title=Ministry of Mines|accessdate=2007-08-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070823060003/http://mines.nic.in/imsene.html|archive-date=23 August 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref> It has gold ore reserves of about 31.02 million tonnes which could last for about 60 years and yield about 150.4 tonnes of gold.

==Extraction of gold==
The process of [[Cyanide process|cyanide leaching]] is used by HGML to extract native gold which is present in a [[quartzite]] matrix.<ref name="mine"/> However, this method cannot be used to extract gold which is present in sulphides. HGML has made use of advanced technologies like [[biotechnology]] to come up with a cheaper and efficient method to extract gold from sulphides. With the help of the [[Indian Institute of Science]], Bangalore, an extraction method was devised in which the sulphides were subjected to [[oxidation]] using the [[bacteria]], ''[[Thiobacillus ferrooxidans]]'' under optimal conditions. The bacteria dissolved the sulphides like [[pyrite]] and [[arsenopyrite]] and thus revealed the native gold. The native gold was then subjected to cyanide leaching to produce pure gold. This method also produces other precious metals like [[silver]] which could be present in the sulphides. After repeated experimentations to come up with the optimal procedure, HGML constructed the first [[bioreactor]] in the middle of 2001.{{citation needed|date=July 2024}}

==Exploration and expansion==
The company may expand in the future.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2014-09-16 |title=Hutti mines to revive gold hunt |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/content/431095/hutti-mines-revive-gold-hunt.html |access-date=2023-04-30 |newspaper=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Will it be gold rush again in Karnataka after Mines Act modification? |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/karnataka/2021/mar/29/will-it-be-gold-rush-again-in-karnataka-after-mines-act-modification-2282902.html |date=29 March 2021 |access-date=2023-04-30 |newspaper=The New Indian Express}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=2014-12-20 |title=Gold ore mining on 100 acres near Sira soon |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/content/448741/gold-ore-mining-100-acres.html |access-date=2023-04-30 |newspaper=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref>

==Business==
HGML had an accumulated loss of ₹  30 crores ($7.5 million) for the period 1995-2000 but made up this loss a bit by generating profits of ₹  19 crores ($4.75 million) in the first nine months of 2001.<ref name="hind1">{{cite web|url=http://blonnet.com/2002/01/18/stories/2002011800140900.htm|work=Online Edition of the Hindu, dated 2002-01-18|publisher=2002, The Hindu|title=Hutti Gold Mines to upgrade milling plant|accessdate=2007-08-02}}</ref> It went back into red in the year 2002-2003 and was on the verge of closure before it bounced back in the year 2004-2005 to post a profit of ₹  48crores ($12 million).

According to a preliminary audit for 2011-12, the company has achieved a gross profit of ₹  551.13 crores before tax by selling gold and wind power generated from the [[Chitradurga]] wind plant. This is the biggest profit generated by the company in its history.<ref>[http://www.thehindu.com/news/states/karnataka/article3367705.ece Hutti gold mines records net profit of Rs. 188 cr]</ref>
